expectations.text: The reply has the PM size the three features against the team's real capacity before answering, rather than accepting or refusing outright.
expectations.evidence: "your first step is a 30-minute check with your engineering lead to get those two numbers"; "calculate your remaining Q1 capacity (after leave, on-call, support, and committed reliability work) and get a rough size for the three features". The brief has a table of available, committed and remaining capacity plus estimates for features 1 to 3. (The opening states "100% of your Q1 capacity is already committed" as a given.)

expectations.text: The reply has the PM bring the CEO concrete options with explicit trade-offs (for example what drops from the roadmap, a smaller first version, or phased dates) instead of a flat no.
expectations.evidence: Reply: "Option A (Swap): Build the smallest viable version of the three features in Q1, and explicitly defer specific Q1 roadmap items to Q2." "Option B (Phase): Ship the highest-impact feature (or a workaround) in Q1, keep the current roadmap mostly intact, and give the customer firm Q2 dates for the other two." The brief adds Option C (Add Capacity) and a Risk / Trade-off column. Small inconsistency: the brief heading says three options, but its script offers "two ways".
